summary.prose: This Story makes one strict module that makes and recognises every artifact id and requirement id, and deletes the second work-item scheme in src/workflow/id.ts together with the throwaway docs migration tool built on it. It also fixes where the folder date comes from: the Epic's creation time is resolved in one head-kind-aware place, the first record any route writes stamps it, and every other record and read path uses the stamp. Path calculations now say whether they are for a read or a write, so the build validation and the completion hook, which compute paths before they persist a record, can anchor a work item on their own turn time, while a genuine read of an unanchored record raises a distinct error that validation surfaces instead of swallowing. New Epic, Story and Task issues carry the artifact id in title and body through all three creation paths, behind an exact-token title lookup on the tracker port. On this branch the 444 stored files with an uppercase story stop resolving until the s9 conversion renames them, so ac1 and k2 must be restated upstream before implementation.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Chosen framework (a1): a shared artifact envelope with typed payloads, stored as a head file plus two append-only sidecar files whose lines carry the owning artifact id, behind a single identity module, with one upfront conversion and no compatibility code. The envelope carries identity, description, parent, references, a typed lifecycle (revision, approval, review, signoffs, staleness, status) and a tracker binding or attachments; the change log and feedback are separate append-only line files; each existing artifact type shrinks to a payload codec and a renderer. Tracker comment reading and attaching are added to the port and implemented for the GitHub adapter only.

ownedContracts.name: ArtifactIdScheme
ownedContracts.purpose: The single place artifact ids are made and recognised: the existing hierarchical typed ids extended for Epic, Story, Task, the Tasks file and diagrams, one story and task form, the folder-name date source, and the functional-requirement id helpers that live in id.ts today.

boundary.internal: The id module and its removal of the second scheme: the folder-name formatter moved into the path scheme, the date source fixed to the epic's creation time, the functional-requirement id helpers and their callers moved with stored FR ids staying valid, issue titles switched to the artifact id, and the delivery module's ordinals. The old issue-body marker is not read. Private to this Story are the exact text of the issue title and the relocation of the helpers.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The envelope model, the one reader and writer, the History API and the sidecar record shape as a contract, and the repository version marker. Private to this Story are the head-file schema, the per-type payload codec registry and how the old per-type read functions delegate to the reader.

The lifecycle rules: status transitions, the revision and content-hash computation, the staleness record, the completion roll-up and the integrity check against the log tail on approve, review and complete. Private to this Story are the hash canonicalisation and how a roll-up is cached or recomputed.

The physical sidecar storage: file layout, the merge attributes for the line files, per-artifact filtering, read-time ordering and de-duplication, and the write order of log entry before head with the repair of a log that is ahead of its head. Private to this Story are the line format and the file naming beside a head.

People-facing feedback: adding feedback and replies from a client, listing open feedback, the addresses rule at revision time, and the per-user identity declaration with alias linking. Private to this Story are the identity file format and the display of linked identities.

The typed binding and attachments, the tracker port additions implemented for GitHub, the retry of pending links and posts, and the switch of unit-issue bookkeeping to the binding. Private to this Story are the permalink construction and the retry bookkeeping.

Task artifacts: creation of the Tasks file and the Task issues at plan approval, direct edits of a Task's own content with local re-approval, refusal of structural edits, and the re-plan reconciliation. Private to this Story are the diff of a Task against the new plan and the build-round recording in a Task's history.

Comment sync: reading human comments into feedback at implement, validate or on request, classifying a revision request or a suggestion from the first line, and posting feedback once. Private to this Story are the first-line commands, the derived since point and the filter for the framework's own posts.

The conversion command: previews, repeats, back-fills history, renames standalone S001 to s1 rewriting the references it can with no alias, creates Epic, Story and Task artifacts for what exists, verifies through the delivery reader, and sets the repository version. Private to this Story are the per-type conversion mappings and the verification report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A — identity and the common model

nonFunctional.performance: Reading an artifact reads its head; the log tail is read only on approve, review and complete, and counts, open feedback and status are computed on read. The delivery loader still reads each artifact once. Loading a repository of about a thousand artifacts must stay within twice today's load time on the same machine.
nonFunctional.security: Gates use the live tracker identity only; declared aliases are never trusted for a decision. The identity file is local and read for attribution. Tracker comments are read through the existing gh path of the GitHub adapter, with no new credential and no direct REST call.
nonFunctional.observability: Every state change appends a change log entry with actor, operation and, where relevant, revision and status; a conflict, a log-ahead-of-head repair, a failed attach and a pending link are logged and surfaced in the unit's result, not hidden.
nonFunctional.durability: Heads are replaced atomically as today; sidecar lines are append-only and de-duplicated by (artifactId, entry id) so a repeated append is harmless; a write appends its log entry before it replaces the head so a failure between the two leaves a detectable, repairable gap; the conversion is one commit, repeatable, and reverts with one git revert.

dataModelChanges.details: The kind set grows by EPIC, STORY, TASK, TASKS and DIAG with a per-kind table of required and forbidden fields; AMD takes the epic hash and a required seq; story and task parts are only s<n> and t<n>. Invariant kept: an existing lowercase-story artifact keeps its id and file name.

defineArtifactId, hldArtifactId, lldArtifactId, planArtifactId, buildArtifactId, specArtifactId, issueArtifactId, codeReviewArtifactId, testsArtifactId and extendArtifactId call ArtifactIds.make instead of interpolating, so a storyId in the uppercase form throws. Invariant broken on purpose: the 444 stored files with an uppercase S0nn no longer resolve until s9; the user's ruling accepts this on v2.

A new standalone story defaults to s1 instead of S001 in the standalone context, the build step defaults ctx.storyId to s1 in implement and validate, and the MCP tool descriptions and examples say s1; a fresh standalone workflow test proves a new routed story passes the strict id check.

WorkflowId, WorkItemIdentity, the minters, toCanonical, toSlug, safeCanonical, parseWorkflowId, deriveWorkItemIdentity, storyIdToOrdinal, taskIdToOrdinal and the FR helpers leave id.ts; the FR helpers move to RequirementIds, the ordinals are read from ArtifactKey, WorkItemIdentity is replaced by WorkItemKey, and the module is deleted. pending.ts shows the artifact id where it showed the canonical work-item id. Invariant kept: parseFrId's successful result shape.

resolveArtifactMdPath and resolveCompanionPath take a WorkItemKey { epicHash, epicCreatedAt, story? } instead of a WorkItemIdentity; workItemRoot builds the root with folderSegment; the storage.ts path builders at lines 726 to 946 and pending.ts deriveMdPath pass a key; the re-exports of the identity constructor and type are removed. Folder text is unchanged.

dataModelChanges.entity: folder date source and epicCreatedAt stamp
dataModelChanges.details: The Epic's creation time is resolved by resolveEpicAnchor alone, by head kind; readEpicDefinitionCore stops returning an LLD's own createdAt; workItemAnchorCreatedAt requires the stamp; finalizeStandaloneLld always stamps; the record-folder helpers take a read or write intent; every other fallback is removed: storage.ts 289 and 505, buildRecordFolderArgs 562-612 and storyRecordFolderArgs 639-651; subject-paths.ts 34; questions.ts 318-341; the callers in test-record.ts and standalone-record.ts; tracker-auto.ts 234 and 495; tracker/link.ts 37; orchestrator.ts 1372, 1847, 2227 and 2687; workflow-rpc.ts 335; synthesize.ts 81; cli/services/workflow.ts 109; pending.ts 201 and 228; delivery/graph.ts 266-287; and the helper callers in gates.ts, chain.ts, implement.ts and validate.ts. Invariant broken on purpose: a read of a record with no anchor now fails before any write instead of choosing its own day.

buildRecordPathsFor, testRecordPaths and storyWorkflowFiles take an explicit PathIntent. runValidateSession (validate.ts) holds one write root for the turn and ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion (completion-record.ts) passes its own now; both call storyWorkflowFiles with write intent before persistBuildRecord. own-files.ts and completion-record.ts are added to the change inventory.

runValidateSession keeps ledger write failures best-effort except MissingAnchorError, which both catches rethrow and which becomes a BuildStepError with code missing-anchor; the TESTS record is still written before the judge, so a judge failure leaves the evidence in place and a retry on a later day files into the same folder.

src/workflow/migrate-docs-tree.ts, its entry src/bin/insrc-migrate-docs.ts with the insrc-migrate-docs bin in package.json, its tests migrate-docs-tree.test.ts and migrate-docs-meta-rewrite.test.ts, its row in src/workflow/artifact-write-inventory.ts and the assertion in artifact-write-inventory.test.ts are deleted: they are built on the second scheme and no compatibility code is kept.
One method findIssuesByTitleToken(token) is added to TrackerPort with a GitHub implementation and a fake; it is the only port change in this Story and overlaps the port additions that s6 owns.

dataModelChanges.entity: unit issue title and body marker

An issue created earlier keeps its title; the old marker is no longer read. Invariant kept: an earlier issue that carries the unit label or an artifact-id title is found.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: This Story owns sc1 and implements ArtifactIds and RequirementIds, including AMD, the folder-name date source and the key-based path scheme. RequirementIds.parse returns the stored shape {date, hash8, story?: number, fr}, not the sketch's {epicHash, ordinal, storyId?}, because a stored requirement id holds only the date and the first 8 hash characters. That change is recorded by the existing pending amendment AMD-2f27754d4ad00b8e-1; the identical amendments -2, -3 and -4 are to be rejected and -1 approved with the user before s2 consumes sc1. The single TrackerPort method findIssuesByTitleToken is an ownership exception between s1 and s6 (s6 owns the port additions in sc6), to be recorded by the user.

errorCases.scenario: A caller passes a story or task in the old uppercase form (S001, T001) to ArtifactIds.make, a storage.ts id function or RequirementIds.mint
errorCases.detection: make and mint test the story against ^s[1-9]\d*$ and the task against ^t[1-9]\d*$ before building the string and throw InvalidArtifactKeyError naming the field and value
errorCases.response: No id is built and nothing is read or written under the uppercase name
errorCases.userImpact: A command run against one of the 444 stored uppercase artifacts fails with a message that points to the s9 conversion instead of silently using a second form

errorCases.scenario: A key breaks the per-kind table: a TASK without a task, a TASKS with a seq, a DIAG or AMD without a seq, an AMD with a story, or a DEF with a story
errorCases.detection: make looks the kind up in a table of required and forbidden fields and compares them with the key's defined fields
errorCases.response: InvalidArtifactKeyError naming the kind and the offending field
errorCases.userImpact: No ambiguous Tasks-file, diagram or amendment id is written

errorCases.scenario: parse is given a folder name <slug>-E<date><hash8>, an E<date><hash8>:S001 work-item id, an uppercase story id or an old issue-body marker
errorCases.detection: parse matches an anchored regular expression per kind and finds no match
errorCases.response: Returns undefined and logs nothing; the caller decides
errorCases.userImpact: A folder name or a work-item id is never taken as an artifact id

errorCases.scenario: A work item is headed by a standalone LLD that has no stamped epicCreatedAt (a record written before this change)
errorCases.detection: resolveEpicAnchor reads the LLD head by kind and finds no stamp; readEpicDefinitionCore no longer falls back to the LLD's own createdAt
errorCases.response: resolveEpicAnchor returns undefined; a write intent anchors with its root, a read intent raises MissingAnchorError, and the s9 conversion stamps old records
errorCases.userImpact: The LLD's own day is never taken as the Epic's creation; an old unstamped item is reported, not guessed

errorCases.scenario: A read-intent path finds no anchor: testRecordMd in validate, the code-review subject path, questions.ts, the pending list or delivery grouping
errorCases.detection: workItemAnchorCreatedAt, or a record-folder helper or path function called with intent kind 'read', finds no stamp and no head and raises MissingAnchorError before any path is computed
errorCases.response: The pending list and delivery grouping catch it per record, log the record id and show the record without a path; questions.ts and the code-review path propagate it; validate returns a BuildStepError with code missing-anchor
errorCases.userImpact: No record is placed in a folder dated the day it was read; the failure is visible

errorCases.scenario: Paths are computed before a BUILD is persisted on the first headless route: storyWorkflowFiles called from validate.ts line 577 or from ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion, with no head, no LLD and no persisted TESTS or BUILD
errorCases.detection: both callers pass intent { kind: 'write', root: { createdAt: rec.meta.createdAt } } and the record-folder helpers take the root when no stamp or head exists
errorCases.response: The paths are computed from the record's own time, the workflow's own files are excluded from the change log, and persistBuildRecord stamps the same time
errorCases.userImpact: A first headless BUILD is written, with a clean change log, instead of failing before the root writer runs

errorCases.scenario: On the first headless validate turn the TESTS write fails for an ordinary reason (disk error) and the judge then succeeds
errorCases.detection: runValidateSession holds one write root { createdAt: now } for the whole turn, so the later storyWorkflowFiles call and persistBuildRecord use it independently of whether the TESTS write persisted an anchor
errorCases.response: The TESTS failure is noted and the verdict is preserved; the BUILD record is written and stamped with the turn's now; the BUILD catch receives no MissingAnchorError
errorCases.userImpact: An ordinary ledger failure does not turn into a missing-anchor error and the verdict is returned

errorCases.scenario: The headless validate flow writes the TESTS record first, then the judge session fails before BUILD is persisted
errorCases.detection: persistTestRecordTask uses write intent with root { createdAt: now }, which stores epicCreatedAt = now in the TESTS record
errorCases.response: The TESTS record is written and stamped; the judge error is returned as today; on a retry on a later day persistBuildRecord finds the TESTS stamp first and files the BUILD in the same folder
errorCases.userImpact: The test evidence is kept and the work item has one folder across days

errorCases.scenario: A ledger write in validate fails for a reason other than a missing anchor (disk full, rename failure)
errorCases.detection: the catch at validate.ts lines 435-439 or 592-597 receives an error that is not a MissingAnchorError
errorCases.response: Logged and noted as today; the verdict is returned unchanged
errorCases.userImpact: A transient write failure does not turn a passing verdict into an error

errorCases.scenario: A MissingAnchorError from a read-intent path reaches one of the two best-effort catches in validate
errorCases.detection: the catch tests error instanceof MissingAnchorError
errorCases.response: Rethrown; runValidateSession returns a BuildStepError with code missing-anchor naming the epic and story, never { next: 'done' }
errorCases.userImpact: A verdict is not reported as successful while a required read failed

errorCases.scenario: The title-token lookup returns more than one issue for one unit
errorCases.detection: ensureUnitIssueDetailed and the tracker-auto push paths check the length of the findIssuesByTitleToken result before they adopt or create
errorCases.response: Returns a failed result naming the token and the issue references, and creates nothing
errorCases.userImpact: A person resolves the duplicate on the tracker; no third issue is created

errorCases.scenario: The title-token lookup or the unit-label lookup fails (gh error, rate limit, offline)
errorCases.detection: the PortResult from the lookup has ok false
errorCases.response: Returns the failure with its kind and creates nothing; a failed lookup is never read as 'not found'
errorCases.userImpact: The push stops with a visible reason and can be repeated

errorCases.scenario: A longer id shares a prefix with the unit's id (STORY-<h>-s10 against STORY-<h>-s1, TASK-<h>-s1-t10 against -t1)
errorCases.detection: the exact-token filter accepts a title only when it equals the token or continues with ' — ' immediately after it, so the character after the prefix decides
errorCases.response: The longer id is not matched and the right unit is adopted or created
errorCases.userImpact: A Story or Task issue is never bound to a different unit

errorCases.scenario: An issue created before this change has an old-scheme title and no unit label
errorCases.detection: neither the unit-label lookup nor the title-token lookup matches it, so the code cannot tell it from a new unit
errorCases.response: The unit is created as new; this is an undetectable residual risk and the result carries no field for it. The s9 conversion relabels old issues
errorCases.userImpact: At most one duplicate per such issue until s9 runs

errorCases.scenario: tracker-auto.ts legacy paths create an issue
errorCases.detection: legacyPushEpic, legacyPushStory and legacyPushTasks obtain their tracker through the createTracker dependency and run the same two lookups before create
errorCases.response: An existing issue is adopted; a new one is created with the unit label, the artifact id title and the marker
errorCases.userImpact: A Story issue made by the legacy path is found again on the next run

errorCases.scenario: folderSegment or RequirementIds.mint receives an invalid time, or mint an ordinal below 1 or a non-integer
errorCases.detection: the parsed date and Number.isInteger(ordinal) are validated before the string is built
errorCases.userImpact: No folder or requirement id with a wrong date is created

errorCases.scenario: A new standalone workflow is started without a storyId
errorCases.detection: standalone.ts reads the storyId parameter and falls to its default, which is now s1
errorCases.response: The story is created as s1 and passes the strict id check
errorCases.userImpact: A freshly routed standalone story does not fail the strict id check

migration.stateBefore: Two id schemes exist. Artifact ids are built by interpolation in src/workflow/storage.ts and by nextAmendmentId in src/workflow/amendments/store.ts (storyId taken as stored, so 444 stored files carry an uppercase S0nn, and new standalone stories, the build-step defaults and the MCP text still say S001). src/workflow/id.ts holds the work-item scheme, WorkItemIdentity and deriveWorkItemIdentity, ordinals that accept both story cases and the requirement-id helpers, and is imported by 15 non-test source files; path-scheme.ts and the storage.ts path builders take a WorkItemIdentity. The folder date is chosen at about thirty call sites with different fallback chains; readEpicDefinitionCore returns an unstamped standalone LLD's own createdAt as the anchor; on the headless build route the TESTS record is written first with its own clock, the path calculations that precede the BUILD persist (storyWorkflowFiles in validate.ts and completion-record.ts) are treated as read-only, and validate.ts swallows ledger write failures. tracker-auto.ts (team and legacy paths), unit-issue.ts and conventions.ts write the work-item id into titles and issue-body markers, TrackerPort can only find issues by label and the legacy tracker-auto paths build their tracker directly. A throwaway docs migration tool built on the second scheme is still in the tree, and four identical pending sc1 amendments exist.
migration.stateAfter: One module makes and recognises every artifact id and requirement id in the strict lowercase form, including AMD, and storage.ts and nextAmendmentId build through it. Every producer defaults to s1. The Epic's creation time is resolved by head kind in one function; the first record any route writes stamps it; the record-folder helpers and the three path functions take an explicit read or write intent, so the validate turn and the completion hook anchor on their own time while genuine reads of an unanchored record raise MissingAnchorError, which validate surfaces as a missing-anchor error instead of swallowing. Paths are built from a WorkItemKey and keep today's folder text. TrackerPort has findIssuesByTitleToken; the three tracker creation paths write the artifact id and guard every create, with an injection seam for the legacy mode. src/workflow/id.ts and the docs migration tool are deleted and nothing refers to them. Artifacts stored with an uppercase story fail with a message that points to the s9 conversion.

migration.backwardCompat: None is kept in code, by the user's ruling. Artifacts already stored in the lowercase form keep their id and file name. The 444 stored files with an uppercase story stop resolving on the v2 branch until the s9 conversion renames them, so ac1 as worded in the DEF cannot hold for them and must be restated upstream, before implementation, as: lowercase artifacts keep their id; uppercase artifacts fail with a pointer to the conversion; and k2 must name the single s9 rename of S001 to s1 as its one exception. A record with no stamped epicCreatedAt, which the old code placed by its own day, now fails on a read path; the s9 conversion stamps it. Issues created earlier keep their title and are adopted by their unit label or an exact artifact-id title; an old issue with neither cannot be recognised by the code and may be duplicated once, which the s9 relabelling avoids. TrackerPort gains one method, which any other implementation of the port must provide. The insrc-migrate-docs command is removed.

alternativesConsidered.name: Strict id module, head-kind-aware anchor, explicit read and write intent, one retained write root per turn
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As the previous design, plus an explicit read or write intent on the path calculations and one write root held for the whole validate turn and the completion hook, so no write-intent caller can be mistaken for a read-only one.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add one identity module with ArtifactIds (per-kind required and forbidden fields including AMD, TASKS and DIAG) and RequirementIds (stored grammar, story a number, undefined on a miss); storage.ts ids and nextAmendmentId build through make. resolveEpicAnchor reads the head by kind (a DEF or ISSUE head contributes its own createdAt, a standalone LLD head only its stamp) and readEpicDefinitionCore stops returning an LLD's own createdAt; finalizeStandaloneLld always stamps; workItemAnchorCreatedAt requires the stamp and raises MissingAnchorError. buildRecordPathsFor, testRecordPaths and storyWorkflowFiles take an explicit intent, either read or write with a root { createdAt }; the write form passes the root to buildRecordFolderArgs and storyRecordFolderArgs, which return the first available of a persisted BUILD or TESTS stamp, resolveEpicAnchor, then the root. Both callers of storyWorkflowFiles are write-intent and pass the record's own createdAt as root: runValidateSession (which holds one root, the turn's now, for the TESTS write, the path calculation and the BUILD persist, so an ordinary TESTS write failure leaves no later step without an anchor) and ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion in completion-record.ts. Genuinely read-only callers (testRecordMd, the code-review subject path, questions, the pending list, delivery grouping) pass read intent and raise MissingAnchorError, which validate rethrows from its best-effort catches as a missing-anchor BuildStepError. WorkItemIdentity is replaced by WorkItemKey, the tracker port gets findIssuesByTitleToken with the exact-token guard and the createTracker seam, the uppercase producers become s1, and id.ts and the docs migration tool are deleted. Restating ac1 and qualifying k2 in the DEF is a prerequisite step before any code change. No amendment proposal is emitted: AMD-1 already records the RequirementIds.parse change.
pros: The first headless route works on the real call order and survives an ordinary TESTS write failure
Read and write intent are explicit in the type, so a write-intent caller cannot silently become read-only
Closes every site the five reviews and the audits found
Does not file another duplicate amendment
cons: Touches about 55 files in one change
Adds an intent parameter to three exported path functions
Adds a TrackerPort method that s6 also touches
Every stored uppercase artifact stops resolving until s9 runs

alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As the previous design, but storyWorkflowFiles catches MissingAnchorError and returns the paths it can compute.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The same id module, anchor resolver, key-based paths and tracker work, but storyWorkflowFiles keeps its existing try and catch style and returns only the paths it can place when the anchor is missing, so no intent parameter is needed.
pros: No change to the exported path function signatures
Smaller change to own-files.ts and completion-record.ts
cons: A first headless BUILD change log would include the workflow's own files because they are not excluded
It hides the missing-anchor condition the Story wants visible
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smaller change but hides the condition and corrupts the first headless change log (partial on ac3).

alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1 for the anchor and paths, but parse and storage lookups keep accepting S001 and map it to s1.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The same anchor and path design as a1, but parse, the storage lookups and the label matcher keep accepting the uppercase story form and normalise it, so the stored artifacts keep resolving until the conversion.
pros: Existing artifacts keep resolving before s9
No window where the repository is unusable
cons: Keeps exactly the compatibility code the user ruled out
Two forms still name one thing in reads
Needs a second change to remove it
